question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Its derivative is given by 

$$
{y}^{′}=-(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\,(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x))+(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡x}\cdot (-\operatorname{cot}⁡x\,\operatorname{csc}⁡x)) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{cot}⁡x \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\operatorname{cot}⁡x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+{cot}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-y\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+{cot}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =-(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+{cot}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =-(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}\frac{1}{\operatorname{csc}⁡x}\,(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+{cot}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =-(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)^{\operatorname{cos}⁡x-1}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+{cot}^{2}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{csc}⁡x)+{cot}^{2}⁡x.$
